All four are correct: Rammohan Roy is linked with the abolition of Sati (1829); the Phules set up a Home for the Prevention of Infanticide (1863); Kandukuri Veeresalingam brought widow remarriage and women's education to Telugu society; and Pandita Ramabai ran a widows' home at Pune. Hence D.

Under Section 2(2) the Hindu Succession Act does not apply to notified Scheduled Tribes. The Supreme Court (8 Oct 2025) upheld this exclusion, so the Act cannot be extended to tribals whatever their religion; it does apply to Scheduled Castes and to residents of Andhra Pradesh generally.
The 2017 amendment raised paid maternity leave from 12 to 26 weeks for women with fewer than two surviving children (at most 8 weeks before delivery); from the third child it stays 12 weeks.

The law was enacted in 1956 as the Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act (SITA) and was renamed the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act by the 1986 amendment. 1986 is the amendment year, not the enactment year; 1961, 1994 and 2003 relate to the Dowry Act, PNDT Act and its renaming.

The Internal Committee is set up in workplaces with 10 or more employees (a-iv) and is presided over by a senior woman employee (c-ii); the Local Committee serves workplaces with fewer than 10 employees (b-iii) and is constituted at district level by the District Officer (d-i). Hence A.
